fair_arrival.title: Open when the kettle boils
fair_arrival.text:
A little courtyard holds a raised pond, a painted booth and a kettle on a dry back counter. The conservatory and kitchen doors have ordinary signs. Mira's aunt, Ada, pours water into the kettle.
Ada: “We are nearly open.”
Mira: “You said that on the postcard.”
Ada: “That was anticipation. This is logistics.”
Mira sets a repaired clockwork boat on the counter, keeping its paper sail clear of the steam.
Mira: “One boat. New spring. Clean shaft. Please don't oil it with whatever you put in the hinges.”
Ada: “The hinges are excellent.”
Mira: “The hinges smell of soup.”
Ada turns a stool toward the pond.
Ada: “Would you like a race? We offer competition, pageantry and approximately two inches of water.”

fair_greeting_ducks.title: The duck declines
fair_greeting_ducks.text:
Ada: “The ducks declined an interview. Very suspicious.”
A painted wooden duck bobs at one corner of the pond. Mira gives it a look, then opens the boat box.
Mira: “We'll start with the boats. They have accessible screws.”

fair_greeting_watch.title: A good viewing spot
fair_greeting_watch.text:
Ada shifts the stool until its feet sit flat and its view of the pond is clear.
Ada: “A discerning audience. Worse than a rival.”
Mira sets a boat at the starting rail.
Mira: “I'll wind it. You can choose the rudder and sail, or leave this one as it is.”

fair_greeting_how.title: Three parts
fair_greeting_how.text:
Mira places one tiny boat beside the other and rests a finger beside its rudder.
Mira: “Three parts. One of them is usually lying to me. The spring moves it, the rudder bends its route, and the paper sail catches the current.”
Ada unrolls a very small starting ribbon.
Ada: “Pageantry is the fourth part. No screws required.”

fair_setup.title: Boats with opinions
fair_setup.text:
The boat sits on the dry starting rail. Mira holds its winding key still while Ada smooths three paper sails with the edge of a postcard.
Mira: “Choose the rudder and a sail, then one winding press. No speed contest with the key.”
The setup menu shows Left / Straight / Right with route arrows. Triangle catches the fixed current; Square is broad and steady; Folded brings the boat round in a circle on a solo run.
You can release your own configuration, watch Mira demonstrate it, or work together on a steady route. You can change your choice before release.
Ada: “The duck has chosen to supervise.”

choices.label: Set a steady route with Mira

fair_crooked.title: A finish at the duck
fair_crooked.text:
Three little boats arc gently toward the same corner. The wooden duck rocks once as their bows arrive. Nothing is damaged.
Ada lifts a blue rosette.
Ada: “A close finish.”
Mira: “They all finished at the duck.”
Ada: “It has an excellent view.”
Mira retrieves the boats from the dry edge and lays yours on a cloth. The rudder is still where it was set. The waterline is higher at one end of the deck.

fair_inspect_boat.title: The rudder tells the truth
fair_inspect_boat.text:
Mira turns the boat over in her palm. She touches the rudder without moving it, then sets the boat back on the cloth.
Mira: “The rudder's where we left it. Let's look at what the boat's standing in.”
Ada leans down to the deck edge. A packing wedge is still tucked beneath one foot.
Ada: “Ah. Yesterday's ambitious sea.”

fair_inspect_wedge.title: Your sea is uphill
fair_inspect_wedge.text:
From the inspection spot, a packing wedge is plainly visible beneath one end of the pond deck. The line of water agrees with it.
You: “Your sea is uphill.”
Ada: “Only at one end.”
She puts the boats safely on the counter, leaving room to shift the wedge from the dry side.

fair_inspect_together.title: A dry-edge investigation
fair_inspect_together.text:
Mira crouches beside the dry deck edge, leaving the inspection spot open beside her. She points to a packing wedge under one foot.
Mira: “Here. The boats aren't all disagreeing independently.”
Ada bends to look at the waterline.
Ada: “A regrettable loss of character. Let's make the sea level.”

fair_inspect_watch.title: Ada notices the waterline
fair_inspect_watch.text:
Ada retrieves a boat, pauses, then holds its hull level beside the slanting waterline.
Ada: “That's not how water usually sits.”
She looks beneath the deck and finds the packing wedge. Mira moves the boat box clear with one foot.
Mira: “We'll leave the duck out of the repair.”

fair_level.title: Shift the wedge
fair_level.text:
The packing wedge raises one foot of the pond deck. The indicator reads TILTED, with a slanted line beside the word.
Mira keeps the boats dry on the counter. Ada steadies the light deck from its safe side.
Ada: “One packing wedge. A whole inland geography.”
One press shifts it into its proper storage slot. The indicator will read LEVEL; there is no balancing or timing test.

fair_leveller_self.title: A level little sea
fair_leveller_self.text:
You slide the wedge into its storage slot while Ada steadies the deck. The water settles against a level line.
Mira retrieves the starting ribbon from Ada's sleeve.
Mira: “There. Now we can disagree with a boat on its own merits.”

fair_leveller_ada.title: Ada adjusts the geography
fair_leveller_ada.text:
Ada shifts the wedge into its storage slot and presses a palm to the deck. The water settles against a level line.
Ada: “We are now offering horizontal water.”
Mira lifts the boat from its cloth.
Mira: “An extravagant improvement.”

fair_ready.title: Horizontal water
fair_ready.text:
The pond indicator reads LEVEL. Ada has stored the wedge beside the boat box; the duck still occupies its corner, with no duties.
Mira puts the winding key within reach and leaves a clear place beside the rail.
Mira: “Same boats. More cooperative sea.”
For a solo run, the rudder and paper sail produce different fixed routes: Triangle catches the current, Square stays steady, and Folded circles. The preview arrows show your choice. Watching uses Mira's demonstration; working together uses a steady middle route.
Ada: “Every route is eligible for precisely the same button.”

choices.label: Set a steady route with Mira

fair_result.title: A button and a sign card
fair_result.text:
Mira takes back the bent brass propeller. She holds it above the boat stall rather than trying to straighten it.
Mira: “If I put this on the sign, at least people will know which stall turns left.”
Ada: “Noor can make you something splendid. Tell her it needs to fit over that door.”
Ada writes the booth's actual width on a card and points to the labelled conservatory door.
Mira: “I also need to tell you something.”
Steam rises visibly from the kettle. Ada lifts a cloth for the handle.
Ada: “And we are open. Could you hold that thought until I've stopped boiling the attraction?”
Mira looks at the dimension card, then tucks it beside the propeller. The fair button is yours on every route.

choices.label: “We can take the sign card over.”
“You can tell her before we go.”

fair_complete.title: Chapter Two complete · The Unfinished Fair
fair_complete.text:
Mira checks a workshop note tucked into her own tool roll: LOWER MILL · BIG CLOCK MECHANISMS.
Mira: “I've chosen a workshop at Lower Mill. Three weeks on the big clock mechanisms. I made that choice myself. I'll tell Ada properly at supper.”
She closes the roll and keeps the sign card with the bent propeller. Ada turns the little OPEN board toward the courtyard.
Souvenirs kept: the Platform 6 ticket and the fair button. Every boat route and the watched race reach this same checkpoint.
Chapter Two is complete. The available build continues into the conservatory. Save and leave here, explore the courtyard, or continue through the conservatory door to make the sign. The conservatory leads onward to supper in the Night Kitchen. Mira’s supper conversation is still ahead in this journey.
You can replay the fair race or close this completion panel and keep exploring the courtyard. Saved progress remains at this checkpoint.

choices.label: Save this chapter · return to courtyard

fair_hours.title: Opening hours
fair_hours.text:
OPEN WHEN THE KETTLE BOILS
CLOSE WHEN I REMEMBER
A small sliding arrow waits beside OPEN. The kettle is on a safe back counter, out of the walkway.
Ada: “The arrow is recent. Before that, people had to inspect the tea.”

fair_prizes.title: The prize shelf
fair_prizes.text:
Four blue rosettes, one button and a jar marked PRESTIGE sit on a shelf. The jar is empty apart from a paper label.
Ada: “Prestige travels well. Doesn't rattle.”
The same little fair button is available after every race route, including watching. The rosettes are part of the display.

fair_bird.title: The painted bird
fair_bird.text:
A wooden bird has been secured with two careful screws. One wing is newly painted. Its beak points slightly down at the booth roof.
Mira looks up while folding the boat cloth.
Mira: “A better place to perch than the hinge. The hinge smells of soup.”
The brush marks and screws are there to look at. The fair can continue without asking about them.

camera_callbacks.take: Mira puts the camera on the dry counter, away from the kettle. “You kept your thumb out of the coast photograph,” she says. “I'm trying to maintain that standard of craftsmanship.” She nudges the boat box clear of the lens.
camera_callbacks.lend: Mira takes the camera from her pocket, then sets it on the dry counter. “I took one wave through the arch,” she says. “No thumb. A modest beginning.” She keeps the lens turned away from the kettle steam.
camera_callbacks.unused: Mira places the still-unopened camera box beside her tool roll, safely away from the kettle. “It made it to the fair unopened. Better packaging discipline than the boats.” She moves the winding key within reach.
camera_callbacks.unselected: Mira lays her tool roll on a dry part of the counter and leaves the winding key within reach. Ada moves the kettle cloth away from the boat box.

outcomes.first:
Your boat crosses first and comes to rest against the soft end rail. Ada awards you the fair button.
Ada: “The rosettes are reserved for ceremonial indecision.”
Mira folds the starting ribbon before it can drift into the pond.
outcomes.second:
Your boat crosses second and rests beside the other two. Ada awards you the fair button.
Ada: “Participation in a navigable body of water.”
Mira: “The water is new to the role. Give it a moment.”
outcomes.third:
Your boat crosses third and rests at the soft end rail. Ada awards you the fair button.
Ada: “Participation in a navigable body of water.”
Mira lifts a strand of starting ribbon from the bow.
Mira: “Pageantry was following it.”
outcomes.circle:
Your boat makes a gentle circle and returns to the near rail. Mira catches its bow against the cloth.
Mira: “A reliable boat. Wrong ambition.”
Ada sets the same fair button beside it.
Ada: “A very thorough inspection of the middle.”
outcomes.spectator:
Mira releases the demonstration boats while you watch from the clear viewing spot. They cross the level pond and settle at the end rail. Ada sets the same fair button within reach.
Ada: “For the audience. It stayed to the end of both turns.”
Mira takes a loose paper sail out of the water and lets it drip onto the cloth.

departures.card:
Mira folds the dimension card once and slips the bent propeller alongside it.
Mira: “Conservatory's through that door. After that, I'm finding supper.”
She points to the labelled door, then waits by the dry starting rail while Ada sets the kettle down.
departures.speak:
Mira looks toward Ada, then back at the card.
Mira: “I can. I want to say it without competing with a kettle. I'll catch her at supper.”
Ada puts the kettle safely on its counter. Mira leaves her conversation for the quieter moment she chose.
departures.wait:
Mira rests her tool roll on the dry rail and watches the duck settle. Ada pours the first cup.
Mira: “Conservatory's through that door. After that, I'm finding supper.”
There is room to wait beside the boats before closing this chapter.
